title: Symmetry-equivariant functional Mirror code generator
hypothesis: With an amortized generator counted as inference state, a symmetry-equivariant m generator achieves <=+0.01 held-out CE vs a byte-near generic m-generator, improves performance after unseen hidden-unit permutations, and saves >=10% total multi-task inference bytes versus full-adapter generation.
physical_object: shared frozen task backbone and a single amortized meta-code generator
mirror_coordinate: task-specific m generated from support data and symmetry-equivariant weight/gradient features
logical_multiplicity: unseen-task functional adapters without one stored dense adapter per task
closest_controls: ordinary MLP hypernetwork / native UNF or NFN / direct learned LoRA task code

requirements.native: Train a generic support-set encoder -> low-rank adapter and a native permutation-equivariant functional network/UNF-style generator -> full adapter. Count the amortized generator size; do not weaken native controls.
requirements.insertion: Replace the generator final head with a k-dimensional m head and a shared fixed task-update basis; feed permutable gradients/weights through an equivariant encoder. Ensure the m output itself is invariant when the requested function is invariant, while intermediate unit-wise outputs transform equivariantly.
requirements.method: For each support set, compute pooled activation and gradient features for a frozen d=32 MLP (2 hidden layers) with explicit neuron-permutation twins. Build small NFN with shared intra-/inter-layer aggregation, plus generic MLP and simple DeepSets baselines; use k={4,8,16}, common base/basis fixed across task families. Independently test exact permutation transport, label-independent feature pipeline and output consistency.
requirements.fixture: Ten source task transformations and six unseen task transformations over class-balanced synthetic classification; each unseen task has 32 support examples, disjoint 128 dev and 256 audit examples; 4 unique permutations of each model for invariance checks.
requirements.hardware: Stage 1 CPU PyTorch float32; optional stage 2 CUDA 1 GPU with transformer if source-only NFN architecture and licenses can be verified.

development.allowed: select code dimension, LR, stop condition only

resources.compute: training examples and updates, FLOPs or MACs, CPU/GPU P50/P95 with batch/dtype/hardware
resources.quality: Few-shot accuracy, CE, m invariance and output equivalence across permutations, actual generator plus basis plus codes bytes, adaptation wall-clock/updates and OOD task identity transfer.

gates.PASS: All five fresh seeds preserve prediction invariance within 1e-4 float32 relative after valid neuron permutation; median held-out loss within +0.01 of best byte-matched m baseline, >=10% full-system byte saving versus UNF-generated full adapters, and no added test-only oracle information.
gates.FAIL: Generic DeepSets/MLP equal or better under matched bytes, broken permutation invariance, or generator cost erases task-code savings.
gates.UNCERTAIN: Missing strong control, uncertain precision, insufficient heldout data, unmeasured runtime or CI overlap

alternative: NFN/UNF parameter sharing is already an effective inductive bias; specialized m may be an information bottleneck and meta-network overhead dominates until many tasks.
uncertainty: Meta-training task diversity, support set draw, permutation group scope, optimizer and model scale; report five seed variation and calibration/test disjointness.
stopping: Stop after 3 dev seeds then 5 fresh worlds; if cheap mechanism fails predeclared gate, record negative and do not tune fresh. Hardware unavailable => BLOCKED (not PASS).
prior_art_delta: Use equivariant neural functionals to emit only low-description m, not full weights, and test byte/transfer gains beyond native UNF and generic hypernetworks.
limitations: Permutation equivariance of an encoder is not itself novel and is not functional multiplicity.
